data.body:
Phase 1 RCA / classification (rebar-debug; read-only code investigation)

Proven mechanism

The reported first transition is real and deterministic: the exact `[operator-attested]` token is part of the acceptance-item TEXT inside `description`. Plan material canonicalization removes checkbox state and insignificant whitespace only; it does not remove semantic item text (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py:90-99,102-134`; `pass1.py:739-778`). Adding the token therefore changes the signed plan-material fingerprint. `compute_validity(..., profile=CLOSE)` rejects the mismatch as `stale-material` (`attest.py:594-620`), and task/story/epic close runs that local plan gate before completion verification (`transition_close.py:341-369`). This is why the completion verifier is not reached on the next close.

Runtime proof

In an isolated temporary real rebar repository, I created an in-progress task, signed a current execution-phase plan attestation, and enabled both close gates. Before editing, `close_plan_review_gate_check` returned `{ok:true, verdict:certified}`. Replacing `- [ ] External ...` with `- [ ] [operator-attested] External ...` changed material `4f3e96f78fcc15a0 -> 7901db5ee4d32d75`; the same check returned `{ok:false, verdict:stale-material}`. A real normal close with both gates enabled exited 1 at the plan gate and left status `in_progress`, proving the ordering rather than an LLM or evidence failure.

The discriminating control used the intended ordering: the exact tag was present before the execution review was signed, then a concrete evidence comment was added afterward. The plan gate remained certified before and after the comment and the material fingerprint was unchanged. This matches the documented rule that comments are non-material. Existing lifecycle coverage also ran green locally (`test_in_progress_self_edit_requires_fresh_execution_review_before_close`): a generic execution self-edit is rejected as stale, a fresh passing execution review restores validity, and normal close succeeds. Therefore there is no unconditional mechanical deadlock in the two gates.

Authority and legitimacy

The staleness behavior is intended, not a code defect. ADR 0043 requires evidence kind to be selected and validated at plan time (`docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md:28-63`) and permits signed completion from a concrete comment only after that classification (`:65-81`). The original close-gate story `unpurified-wolflike-flycatcher` explicitly requires current own material, says own-material drift always invalidates even when pin enforcement is off, orders the plan gate before completion, and prescribes a separate `review-plan`; the shipped contract repeats this at `docs/plan-review-gate.md:455-479,495-520,906-955`. ADR 0052 protects re-review stability only for byte-identical plans (`docs/adr/0052-plan-review-validation-consistency-and-re-review-stability.md:41-48`), not a late semantic retag. Normalizing this token out of plan material would contradict the original anti-tamper intent because it changes which evidence bar completion applies.

The stronger claim that a fresh review can never pass is conditional, not a gate deadlock. It occurs when the old implementation plan has become factually obsolete after delivery. On `amoebic-random-spoonbill`, the recorded fresh reviewer correctly observed that `bug_close_reason_ok` no longer exists; a current source sweep also finds zero occurrences of that symbol or `build_acli_client_from_env`. A truthful current plan can be re-reviewed and close mechanically, as the lifecycle control proves. If no truthful current execution plan can pass because the work is already over, force-close preserving an unsigned signal is the designed escape hatch.

Design conflict / residual defect

There is a genuine cross-contract guidance conflict, but it does not authorize changing either gate automatically. `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` tells an untagged external-evidence caller to add the exact token and comment, then re-verify (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py:48-64`). Ticket `grained-grassgreen-tench`, which deliberately clarified that wording after the close-plan gate shipped, states the same sequence but does not mention that retagging invalidates plan material or requires a fresh current execution review first. For delivery-consumed plans, the two explicit policies cannot both be satisfied without choosing which assurance to weaken or adding a new representation for evidence kind.

Classification: the reported gate behavior is **intended-behavior / design conflict**, not an automatic bug repair under the original-epic-intent rule. The exact original intents favor early evidence-kind classification plus material invalidation. The completion-remediation message is composition-incomplete and should be addressed only after a design decision: preserve anti-tamper and teach late-tag callers to re-plan or force-close; allow a narrowly defined evidence-kind migration; or represent reviewed evidence kind outside mutable description text. No code was edited, no ticket was claimed or transitioned, and no other tracker record was changed.
